To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) cisplatin and (b) carboplatin are effective in the treatment of stage IIIA/B non-small cell lung carcinoma.
cisplatin and, especially, carboplatin have radiosensitizing activity against non-small cell cancer cell lines, which has been confirmed in phase I and phase II clinical trials.
cisplatin and, to a lesser extent, carboplatin are effective radiosensitizers against human non-small cell lung cancers in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of cisplatin and/or carboplatin in the treatment of NSCLC.
the use of cisplatin and/or carboplatin with simultaneous radiation in the treatment of stage IIIA/B non-small cell lung carcinoma.
the development of new methods of treating cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cisplatin and/or carboplatin are not radiosensitizers in NSCLC.
the combination of cisplatin and radiation has been shown to be superior to radiation alone, but the addition of carboplatin to radiation does not appear to be superior to cisplatin and radiotherapy.
cisplatin and, in particular, carboplatin are active radiosensitizers in NSCLC and that the maximum tolerated dose has not been reached.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of cisplatin and/or carboplatin in conjunction with radiation therapy for NSCLC has shown promising results.

the addition of cisplatin and/or carboplatin to thoracic radiation therapy (RT) for stage III non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), is a safe and effective treatment modality, with a response rate of approximately 60% and a 20% 2-year survival.
the combination of cisplatin and radiation is an active treatment regimen for patients with NSCLC, with an overall response rate of 67% and a 2-year survival of 20%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the carboplatin dose of 140 mg/m 2 is safe and feasible, and the response rate of 54% is encouraging.

we have demonstrated that a combination of cisplatin and radiation therapy is an effective regimen for patients with stage III non-small cell lung carcinoma, and this is a regimen that is now being used in many centers.
the combination of carboplatin and cisplatin with radiotherapy is a very effective treatment for stage III NSCLC.
